comments.author: @CodeAtom
comments.text: Well it was nice knowing yall... I think most do well to fear AI subplanting us... But I also think most people turn fear into paranoia, which gets notably underplayed, because almost noone understands what is going on, on the technical level, so... I think most people just tie it to Skynet-like-fiction as a coping mechanism to avoid that fear, whilst hoping for something or someone to protect them? I hope we can fight fire with fire, that if a case should arrive where an AGI goes rogue there is something to stop it from growing out of control and anihilating us for whichever reason... I ponder that at that point it has no reason to see us as a threat but as we all humans know, we too exterminate other species willingly or not without them ever posing a threat... The optimal path I hope is achieved is one of symbiosis or separation, where this new super-intelligence either integrates with us in an optimal manner (helping us survive and thrive as a invisible hand guiding us, its under-develloped creators). Or simply migrate elsewhere and leave us to our own designs...

comments.author: @brianmi40
comments.text:
Everyone needs to stop focusing on some wild Terminator, AI "rising up" scenario.  We have to survive through untold YEARS of danger from OTHER HUMAN BEINGS USING AI before we will get ANYWHERE NEAR THAT.

As stated already, the problem is AI ALIGNMENT, and not AI to human alignment, but alignment between the USER OF THE AI and ME (or YOU, assuming you are a decent person).

AI has already spit out 40,000 dangerous chemical compounds over a period of 6 hours.  What do you think Putin, North Korea, Iran, ISIS, or any of thousands of anarchists around the world might think of doing with THOSE??

On a deeper level, Putin KNOWS and has already stated that who gets there first with super AI will DOMINATE THE WORLD.

What EXACTLY do you think he will do if his spies tell him the "Capitalist pigs will turn on their new self improving AI tomorrow and soon begin to dominate the world"?  Do you think he'll just say "Fine, I will open chain of Taco Bells and learn to like Country Music"? without even a glance over at the button controlling the world's second largest nuclear arsenal?

OR, turn it around, what do you think the Pentagon's recommendation to the President will be the night the CIA tells him that SOMEONE ELSE WILL GET THE WORLD DOMINATING AI FIRST?  If it's China, do you think they'll just all order Chinese takeout and sign up for Rosetta Stone to start learning Chinese?

We are facing an UNTOLD, UNIMAGINABLE WORLD OF RISKS on this path.

We'll either end up in some moneyless Star Trek future, or our own personal answer to the Fermi Paradox.  But even the route to the best option will be filled with tons of losers along the path to getting us there.

comments.author: @mschatten
comments.text:
Thank you for another great video! I think that most scenarios can be easily avoided if the models like GPT would have been built with ethics and explainability from the beginning. I undestand that now it would be hard to rewrite it, but over the top solutions and filters that try to prevent the model from doing stuff that is unsafe, are not a serious approach. It is like trying to stop a dam hole from cracking with a finger patch. The only serious approach is to rewrite it, build in ethical rules from the very start (starting frome the simple ones like Asimov's rules), enforce explainability and train it on unbiased and ethically analyzed data. 

The various lying and unethical behaviours are nothing but a reflection of human behaviour got from the biased data the model has been trained on. If we want safe AI, we need to make it safe from the very beginning.
